text:
Maya Chen: secops-bot just alerted to a public ACL on a GCS bucket that contains build artifacts and a service-account key. link: https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/redwood-temp-artifacts
secops-bot: Alert: storage.bucket.acl.public (policy match=PUBLIC_READ) on projects/redwood-prod/buckets/redwood-temp-artifacts at 2026-03-20T09:04:10Z
Jon Rivera: oof. which objects? any keys detected in the objects?
Maya Chen: one object named deploy/service-account.json looks like a SA key blob. size ~2.1KB.
Li Patel: can someone run a quick gsutil ls -L and grep for the file metadata so we know when it was created?
Carter S: running: ```gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-temp-artifacts/deploy/```
Carter S: output shows: "Creation time: 2026-03-20T08:52:43Z", ACL: AllUsers:R (OBJECT)
Sam Irwin: timeline check: was that file touched by the nightly build? build pipeline ID #2381 ran at 08:50. pinging CI owners. @Jon Rivera can you check pipeline logs?
Jon Rivera: CI logs show a step `gsutil cp build/service-account.json gs://redwood-temp-artifacts/deploy/` in a deploy debug step. It should have been using a temp key but looks like a persisted key got checked in to the workspace.
Maya Chen: containment plan: 1) make bucket private 2) revoke the exposed service account key 3) scan for other occurrences 4) rotate KMS keys if used 5) comms. Agree? :eyes:
Li Patel: agree. proposed commands: ```gsutil defacl set project-private gs://redwood-temp-artifacts && gsutil acl ch -r -d AllUsers gs://redwood-temp-artifacts```
Carter S: doing bucket lockdown now. running commands...
secops-bot: Action log: permission change requested by Carter S at 2026-03-20T09:06:22Z
Carter S: done. bucket defacl set to project-private and removed AllUsers ACL on objects. verifying: ```gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-temp-artifacts/deploy/service-account.json``` shows no public ACLs now.
Maya Chen: next revoke the compromised key. we need the key ID from the JSON blob — can someone paste the private_key_id field?
Jon Rivera: pasted the JSON, private_key_id = "9f2a4cabcdeexample". running: ```gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=ci-robot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com``` to find matching key.
Sam Irwin: found match. revoking now: ```gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 9f2a4cabcdeexample --iam-account=ci-robot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com```
secops-bot: Action log: revoked key 9f2a4cabcdeexample for ci-robot@redwood-prod at 2026-03-20T09:09:03Z
Li Patel: add remediation: rotate any CI tokens that used that key, update pipeline to use short-lived tokens or Workload Identity.
Maya Chen: I want an inventory scan for any other buckets or repos with that private_key_id or the SA email. Carter, can you run a quick `gsutil -m` grep across buckets and then an internal code search?
Carter S: kicked off `gcloud storage objects list --project=redwood-prod --format='value(name)' --bucket=* | xargs -n1 gsutil cat | grep -E "ci-robot@redwood-prod|9f2a4cabcdeexample"` (will take a bit). also queued a repo search across monorepo for the email.
Jon Rivera: CI owners: we need to revoke any long-lived credentials and change CI job to use Workload Identity Federation. I'll file a quick PR to replace copy-step with `gcloud auth print-identity-token` approach.
Maya Chen: good. operational asks for infra: 1) enable Data Access audit logs for storage.googleapis.com on the project 2) require CMEK for sensitive buckets (we use KMS key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/keys/cmek-artifacts) 3) deny public acl via org policy: `constraints/storage.allowedPublicBuckets`
Li Patel: I can open the org policy request. For CMEK, we should enable bucket-level holds and require CMEK for new buckets via Terraform.
Sam Irwin: post-incident checklist: rotate any KMS keys if the credential allowed KMS access, run a service account permissions audit, and add a pre-commit check to disallow JSON SA keys in builds.
Maya Chen: communications: draft a short incident note for internal slack + security channel and an email to affected teams. treat as P2 — no evidence of exfil yet but assume keys in plaintext were accessible while public.
Carter S: scan results: found one other object with same SA email in a `tmp/` folder uploaded by a developer at 2026-03-18. removed and notified the owner. no other matches in repos so far.
secops-bot: Remediation checklist created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-7421 (assignee: Maya Chen)
Jon Rivera: CI changes merged to prevent copy of raw keys (workload identity PR #402).
Li Patel: org policy change submitted (PR #12) to disallow public buckets; awaiting infra review.
Maya Chen: closing loop: bucket ACL locked, key revoked, CI patched, scans in progress, org policy + audit logs requested. next steps: 24h monitoring for anomalous access and full blameless postmortem tomorrow 1400. thanks all. :thumbsup:
